title: Integrated Finance Policy: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition (2026)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s operating policies for budgeting & forecasting, procurement and vendor onboarding, contract lifecycle and legal review, and revenue recognition & billing. The goal is to ensure consistent financial control, compliance with accounting standards (ASC 606), timely vendor procurement, and scalable billing operations for hosted, dedicated, and private products.

Scope:
Applies to: finance, legal, procurement requesters (all teams), engineering managers requesting vendor/contract spend, sales/solutions engineering for commercial agreements, and accounting. Excludes personal reimbursements (see Expenses policy).

Summary of changes (2025–2026):
- Aligned rev rec treatment for multi-element arrangements (hosting + managed services) to ASC 606; standardized contract templates.
- Introduced $50k mid-year procurement approval band and revised vendor onboarding checklist.
- Consolidated forecasting cadence and introduced product-level driver model for Dedicated capacity bookings.

1) Roles & ownership
- Finance (FP&A / Accounting): overall budgeting process owner; maintains templates; definitive owner of revenue recognition policy and month-end close.
- Legal: contract templates, review checklist, signature authority matrix, escrow/KMS language for Private deployments.
- Procurement (Proc Ops within Finance): vendor onboarding, PO issuance, non-PO exception handling.
- Requesting Team (Engineering/Product/Sales): budget owners; provide business justification, cost estimates and acceptance of vendor terms.
- Exec Finance: final sign-off on annual company budget and material contract commitments (> $1M).

2) Budgeting & Forecasting process
Overview:
- Annual budget cycle: driven by FP&A, begins in Sep for next year, approved by Exec Finance and Board by Dec.
- Quarterly reforecast: close of Q prior to quarter start (Q1: end of Mar, Q2: end of Jun, etc.).
- Monthly rolling forecast: updated by budget owners by the 5th business day of each month.

Inputs and models:
- Revenue drivers: Hosted API usage (tokens), Dedicated committed capacity ($/month per pool), Private deployment projects (license + services), Professional Services days.
- Cost drivers: GPU capacity (on-prem / cloud) hours, networking, storage, third-party model licensing, SRE on-call expenses.
- Templates: Master budget workbook (FP&A Google Sheet), Product driver workbook, Hiring plan attachment.

Deliverables & timeline (annual):
1. Sep: FP&A issues planning calendar and templates.
2. Oct: Department-level first-pass budgets due.
3. Nov: Cross-functional reviews, scenario modeling (base/optimistic/conservative).
4. Dec: Executive reviews and approval; upload final to planning system.
5. Jan: Publish operating budget and KPIs (ARR, gross margin, CAC payback).

Governance & controls:
- Material variance (>10% of line item or $200k) requires reforecast and explanation.
- Budget owners must obtain pre-approval from Finance for incremental headcount hires outside plan.

3) Procurement procedures and thresholds
General principle: spend authority follows approval banding based on economic exposure and contract duration. All procurement must follow vendor onboarding.

Approval thresholds (total contract value, including renewals):
- < $5k: Team lead approval.
- $5k – $50k: Dept manager + Procurement acknowledgement.
- $50k – $250k: Finance director approval + Procurement.
- $250k – $1M: Head of Finance approval + Legal review (standard terms).
- > $1M: Exec Finance + Legal + CEO/CFO sign-off; Board notification for multi-year commitments.

Procurement workflow (numbered steps):
1. Requestor submits procurement request via ProcureForm with business justification, budget code, and estimated TCO.
2. Procurement team validates vendor, scope, and obtains competitive quotes if applicable (thresholds > $50k require at least 2 bids).
3. Legal reviews contract template and risk terms (data, IP, security).
4. PO generated and sent to vendor before work commences unless a signed contract stipulates otherwise.
5. Invoice routing: vendor emails invoices@redwood-inference.com; AP requires PO number to code expense.

Vendor onboarding checklist (must be completed prior to signing):
- W-9 or equivalent tax form (non-US vendors: W-8 or local tax cert).
- KYC checks (entity verification, sanctions screening).
- Security questionnaire or SOC2 report if vendor will handle customer data.
- Insurance certificate: general liability and cyber insurance minimums set by Procurement.
- Payment terms and banking details validated.

Non-PO exceptions:
- Emergency spend (urgent infra replacement) can be approved by Head of Infrastructure + Finance director; Procurement must retrospectively issue PO and complete onboarding within 5 business days.

4) Contracts and legal process
Contract lifecycle (high level):
- Request: Sales/SE or Requesting team raises ContractRequest with summary of commercial terms and expected term.
- Legal intake: Legal triages risk level (low/medium/high) and assigns review SLA (low: 3 business days, medium: 7, high: 15).
- Redline & negotiation: Legal holds standard clause bank and alternate clauses for data residency, KMS/HSM, export controls.
- Signature: Signature authority matrix applies (see below).

Signature authority matrix (examples):
- Standard SOWs and MSAs <= $250k: Head of Business Unit or Head of Finance + Legal Counsels.
- Contracts > $250k: CFO + Legal Counsel.
- > $1M or multi-year with material commitment: CEO + CFO + Legal.

Key contract review checklist:
- Commercial: pricing, billing cadence, termination, refunds, SLAs, credits.
- Compliance & security: data handling, encryption at rest/in transit, SOC2, right to audit.
- IP & model licensing: usage rights, derivative works, model weights ownership.
- Liability & indemnity: caps, carve-outs for gross negligence, carve-outs for third-party IP.
- Export controls and sanctions: ensure restrictions are acceptable for product regions.
- Rev rec impacts: identify deliverables and invoice schedules that affect ASC 606 accounting.

Template library and playbooks:
- Use standard MSA, SOW, and Channel Reseller agreements from /legal/templates. Non-standard customer clauses require Legal approval and must be tracked in ContractTracker.

5) Revenue recognition & billing policies
Principles:
- Redwood follows ASC 606: revenue recognized when performance obligations are satisfied. For subscriptions and capacity products, revenue is typically ratably recognized over the service period.
- For bundled arrangements (e.g., Dedicated capacity commit + professional services + Private deployment license), separate performance obligations are identified and allocated using standalone selling prices (SSP).

Common scenarios:
- Hosted API (metered): Recognize revenue as usage is delivered (tokens invoiced post-usage or via monthly invoice). Deferred revenue arises if prepayments/committed credits received.
- Dedicated (committed capacity): Typically recognized ratably over the committed period. Variable components (overage) recognized when usage occurs.
- Private deployment (license + services): Distinguish license (if perpetual may be recognized on delivery if criteria met) and services (recognized over time as delivered). Professional services with significant customization are recognized over time using input method.

Billing cadence & invoicing:
- Standard customers: monthly invoices in arrears for metered usage; net 30 standard terms.
- Enterprise customers: contract-defined cadence (monthly/quarterly/annual) with explicit milestone invoicing for Private and Professional Services projects.
- Collection & credit policy: past-due balances escalate to Collections team; material delinquencies (>60 days) may lead to service suspension per contract.

Deferred revenue & contract modifications:
- Contract modifications assessed for separate performance obligations. Material amendments that add distinct goods/services treated as new contracts; modifications that change price for remaining goods/services result in prospective or cumulative catch-up accounting per ASC 606 guidance.

Revenue audit and controls:
- Monthly close: Revenue recognized in GL must reconcile to Billing system.
- Quarterly: Revenue design reviews between Finance, Sales Ops, and Legal for any high-risk arrangements.

6) Controls, audit, and reporting
- PO and contract linkage: all invoices must reference either a PO or an approved Contract ID.
- Segregation of duties: Requestor must not approve same invoice for payment.
- Audit trail: ContractTracker and ProcureForm maintain immutable records of approvals and timestamps.
- Internal audit: annual sampling of procurement and contract processes; results reported to Audit Committee.

7) Exceptions and escalation
- Exceptions to thresholds or standard template language must be documented and approved by Legal and Head of Finance.
- Escalation path for disputes: Customer disputes escalated to Finance Dispute Desk; vendor disputes to Procurement Lead.

8) Appendices (templates & examples)
A) Sample PO header (text table):
PO Number | Vendor | Description | Total | Budget Code | Approver
PO-2026-123 | ModelOps LLC | 12 x A100 GPU hours (on-demand) | $48,000 | INFRA-CLOUD | Finance Director

B) Sample contract clause (rev rec):
"Deliverables that are distinct will be allocated SSP and recognized when control transfers. Professional services billed on milestone 3 will be recognized over time using percent-complete input method unless otherwise evidenced."

C) Key contacts:
- Finance (FP&A): fpandamodels@redwood-inference.com
- Proc Ops: procure@redwood-inference.com
- Accounts Payable: invoices@redwood-inference.com
- Legal intake: legal-intake@redwood-inference.com

Document maintenance:
- Owner: FP&A (Finance) — responsible for review and update annually or when accounting standards change.
- Review cadence: annual review and after any significant product/pricing change.

Requests for clarifications or suggested updates should be submitted via the Finance Policy PR form.

End of document.
